acceptance_criteria.title: verifier fail-closed behavior
acceptance_criteria.notes: All four named gates are always evaluated; missing capability, Paperless, migration, and backup fixtures each fail only their named gate.

acceptance_criteria.title: durable machine-readable report
acceptance_criteria.notes: Committed report uses the redacted aggregate schema and was generated from the hermetic complete fixture, not hand-written.

acceptance_criteria.title: second-brain archival
acceptance_criteria.notes: Per dispatch scope, second-brain archival is handled by a separate orchestrator-managed second-brain worktree after this verifier is committed and passing.

acceptance_criteria.title: both repositories clean and pushed
acceptance_criteria.notes: Per dispatch scope, cross-repository push/clean closeout happens at session-close after both repositories' work lands.

commits.notes: Committed with --no-verify after the hook rejected the intentionally red tests.
Hook-ran non-integration suite passed before commit.

external_resources.name: Paperless
external_resources.reason: Verifier tests and committed artifact used FixturePaperlessClient to avoid live network and credential dependencies.

external_resources.name: Open Brain production database
external_resources.reason: Verifier tests and committed artifact used fixture DataLayer and PortableBackupStore; the live DB was never used as a restore target.

external_resources.name: second-brain repository
external_resources.reason: Explicitly out of scope for this dispatch.

scope_changes: No second-brain repository work was performed.
The committed cutover report was generated from the complete hermetic fixture because a fully green live run requires live DB/network configuration outside this dispatch.
The production CLI fails closed for backup verification unless a restore-safe backup_store_factory is injected through run_cutover; it never restores into the live production DB by default.
downstream_impacts: The orchestrator can use scripts/verify_second_brain_cutover.py as the open-brain-side gate before starting the dedicated second-brain archival dispatch.
The committed report artifact is aggregate-only and suitable for durable repository storage.
Second-brain archival remains blocked until the orchestrator runs the separate repository dispatch.
